testcase.name: the bytes are verified once before the switch and the cheap check is used after it()
server app manual rollback - the site switch fails after the runtime moved - the runtime goes back, the active release is unchanged()
after a worker restart the release that was active BEFORE the switch is still the rollback target()
a rollback checks the target's bytes before the switch and only the cheap check after it()
an artifact whose bytes were altered is never switched in()
server app publish - unhealthy after the switch also puts the runtime back, even when the pointer had not moved()
the order is verify the artifact, stage, switch, confirm - nothing serves before it was verified()
N+1 is unhealthy after the switch - rolled back, with the health detail as the reason()
a rollback never clobbers a newer release that was switched in the meantime()
a release that cannot be verified because the check itself failed is not served either()
a healthy new release becomes the live one and the happy path writes no extra history()
the first release has nothing to go back to - a failure leaves the site serving nothing, said explicitly()
an answer that cannot be trusted is not success - unknown verification rolls back and is marked ambiguous()
server app manual rollback - a runtime that will not start leaves everything as it was()
N+1 switches then fails - N is active again from its own artifact and nothing is rebuilt()
repeating the rollback is safe - the second run finds the pointer is no longer ours and touches nothing()
server app publish - the switch fails after the runtime moved - both go back to the previous release()
a release without any artifact cannot be restored()
server app first release - a failure after the runtime started stops it again()
manual rollback that the provider refuses changes nothing and says so()
server app publish - a runtime that does not start leaves the site and the runtime on the previous release()
automatic rollback - the previous artifact disappears between the check and the confirmation - fail closed, not a pointer at nothing()
a provider that cannot stage the release leaves the serving release untouched()
manual rollback verifies the artifact first, needs no build, and repeating it changes nothing()
an app without a server part never touches the runtime()
a provider that fails before it switched anything leaves the active release alone()
a first release that cannot be verified never serves anything - no switch, so nothing to take offline()
server app publish - the server runtime serves the new release before the site pointer moves()
automatic rollback failure fails closed - the pointer is NULL, never at the release that just failed or at a missing artifact()
a provider that cannot restore is a recorded rollback failure, not a silent one - and it says the site could not be taken offline either()
server app manual rollback - static and runtime cannot be reconciled - offline and inconsistent, never success()
server app - when the runtime cannot be put back the site is taken offline, never a mixed release, and it is not reported as a rollback()
an artifact that cannot be verified is never switched in - the serving release is untouched and nothing is recorded as switched()
manual rollback - the artifact is verified, then disappears before the switch is confirmed - not success, the active release is unchanged()
server app manual rollback - the runtime goes to the target first, then the site, and both end on the same release()
a deploy timeout is ambiguous - not success, not retried, previous release restored()
